questions.stem: A facility discards a spent solvent mixture. What is the first regulatory management decision?
options: Select a disposal vendor before identifying the waste
Assume it is nonhazardous because it was useful when purchased
Dilute it until the concentration appears lower
Determine whether the discarded material is a solid waste and whether it is hazardous under applicable rules
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The generator must identify each waste stream and make an accurate hazardous-waste determination using process knowledge or appropriate analysis.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A generator must identify and characterize the waste before selecting compliant management and disposal.
Product status before use does not determine waste classification after discard.
Dilution is not a substitute for hazardous-waste determination and may be prohibited treatment.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 27, hazardous waste and governing regulations, pp. 616-629; 40 CFR 262.11

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the hazardous-waste manifest system?
options: Track regulated hazardous waste from the generator through transportation to the designated facility
Replace the waste determination
Authorize employees to enter confined spaces
Classify workplace chemical labels under GHS
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The manifest provides cradle-to-grave shipment documentation and accountability among generators, transporters, and receiving facilities.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The manifest follows a waste already identified; it does not make the initial determination.
Confined-space authorization is governed by a separate safety program.
Hazard communication labels serve workplace chemical information, not waste shipment tracking.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 27, RCRA and hazardous waste operations, pp. 622-629; 40 CFR Part 262

questions.stem: What determines whether a federal hazardous-waste generator is a very small, small, or large quantity generator?
options: The total number of employees at the company
The amount and type of hazardous waste generated in a calendar month
The physical size of the facility
The annual sales revenue
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Federal generator categories are based on monthly generation quantities, including separate thresholds for acute hazardous waste.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Employee count does not establish the federal generator category.
Facility area does not determine the category.
Revenue is not the classification basis.
questions.sourceTitle: US EPA Hazardous Waste Generator Regulatory Summary
questions.sourceLocation: EPA hazardous-waste generator regulatory summary; Yates Chapter 27

questions.stem: A corrosive hazardous waste is placed into a metal drum that reacts with the waste. What control principle was violated?
options: Every hazardous waste must be stored only in glass
Labeling removes the need for compatibility review
The container material must be compatible with the waste and maintained in good condition
A reaction is acceptable if the container is outdoors
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Waste containers must be suitable for the material so corrosion, reaction, leakage, pressure, and loss of containment are prevented.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Compatible materials vary with the waste; glass is not universally required or suitable.
A label communicates hazards but does not prevent chemical attack.
Outdoor location does not make a reactive container system safe or compliant.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 27, hazardous-material properties, storage, and site control, pp. 619-632

questions.stem: An oxidizer and an organic solvent are stored together because both fit in the same cabinet. What is the strongest correction?
options: Keep them together but add a flammable-liquid label
Store them on the same shelf with the oxidizer above the solvent
Rely on employee memory to prevent mixing
Segregate incompatible materials using compatibility information and suitable secondary containment
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Storage design should prevent incompatible chemicals from contacting one another during normal handling or a release.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A label does not prevent incompatible contact during leakage or handling.
Vertical arrangement does not provide adequate separation and may worsen spill contact.
Memory is unreliable and does not create engineered segregation.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 27, hazardous material properties, fires, explosions, and storage, pp. 619-629

questions.stem: A spill exceeds employee training and available protective equipment and is moving toward a drain. What is the best immediate decision?
options: Isolate the area, initiate the emergency plan, and use qualified responders
Direct unprotected employees to absorb the spill quickly
Wash the material into the drain to remove it from the floor
Wait until the material reaches the property boundary
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: An uncontrolled release beyond incidental-spill capability requires emergency notification, isolation, and appropriately trained response resources.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Employees should not perform response beyond their training, equipment, and assigned role.
Discharging the material can spread exposure and create environmental violations.
Delay increases migration and consequence.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 27, hazardous waste operations, emergency planning, and site control, pp. 629-633

questions.stem: Why is a contamination-reduction zone established between the hot zone and support zone?
options: To increase the time responders remain exposed
To control movement and remove contamination before personnel and equipment enter clean areas
To store incompatible wastes together
To eliminate the need for respiratory protection in the hot zone
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Controlled work zones and decontamination prevent contaminants from being carried into support areas and communities.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The zone is intended to reduce spread, not extend exposure.
Waste compatibility controls still apply.
Hot-zone PPE and respiratory protection remain based on the hazard assessment.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 27, site control and decontamination, pp. 629-633

questions.stem: A waste stream contains several process chemicals. How should the safety professional use supplier SDS information?
options: Treat the original product SDS as a complete waste characterization
Ignore all SDS information after a product becomes waste
Use it as one input, then evaluate the actual waste composition, reactions, and process history
Use only the product trade name to select disposal
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Waste characterization integrates process knowledge, analytical data when needed, and reliable hazard information rather than relying on a single document.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The waste may contain mixtures, contaminants, or reaction products not represented by one product SDS.
SDS information can still help identify constituents, incompatibilities, and controls.
Trade names do not provide enough information for a defensible determination.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 27, hazardous-material properties and classification, pp. 616-629

questions.stem: Drums of liquid hazardous material are stored near a storm drain. Which improvement most directly limits release migration?
options: Increase the font size on inventory labels
Move the inspection log to a nearby office
Require two employees to sign each delivery
Provide compatible secondary containment and protect or isolate the drainage pathway
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Secondary containment and drainage control interrupt the pathway from a failed primary container to soil, water, and public systems.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Labeling supports communication but does not capture a leak.
Record location does not control physical migration.
Signatures do not provide containment.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapters 27 and 34, site control, containment, and environmental protection, pp. 629-633 and 754-778

questions.stem: Which action is highest in a waste-management hierarchy?
options: Redesign the process to prevent or reduce hazardous waste generation at the source
Ship all waste to a disposal facility
Add water to increase the waste volume
Store the waste indefinitely on site
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Source reduction avoids generation and usually provides stronger environmental and risk benefits than treatment or disposal.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Disposal manages waste after generation and is lower in the hierarchy.
Dilution increases volume and does not prevent hazardous constituents.
Indefinite storage creates accumulating risk and does not eliminate the waste.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
